notes.text: The page refines graph weighting by a family R_a with orientation-dependent cyclic permutations. It gives an equivalent torsor description and the construction R_a = R intersect tilde Sigma_a. These are transcribed statements; no mathematical proof was checked.
The live NB uses r(omega), twice, although the preceding map is written r:A to N. The visibly written omega is preserved, without substituting a.
The top author page number is 6; a separate handwritten 49 is present at the lower-left corner. Both are retained.

The cancelled initial formula and the lower square each use a vertical equality drawn as two short parallel strokes. In the initial formula the lower rightward arrow is the vector accent of A; it is not a second downward arrowhead.

The cancelled phrase before R/alpha contains residual strokes that admit two word segmentations. The proposal retains both: a first reading with one provisional unreadable unit and a second une, and the shorter C reading. The unreadable-unit count is provisional and the complete line is supplied for independent audit.

The original was viewed once, each supplied half once, and twenty-two distinct enlarged evidence crops once each. All live agreement text and symbols were read. Physical line count includes insertions, diagram rows, isolated formula rows and the two handwritten numbers. No OCR, web source or TeX compilation was used.

Independent second reading restores an additional cancelled remplacée; favours triple and correspondant in two crossed replacements while retaining alternatives; and reads the underlined cancelled noun injection literally after application. The lower old equation has ell and a partial/alpha-C argument, not the first draft R/π₀ alternatives. No mathematical repair is made to these cancelled fragments. The local r notation is confirmed from the clearer NB occurrences; r(omega) is retained literally. Cancellation extent, a lower de/deux attachment, a compressed abbreviation, and the bottom square’s arrowhead/accent remain explicit uncertainties.
